notice: SAMPLE PLAN, for illustration only. The existence of this JSON file, and any script (including scripts/bin/validate-plan.mjs) successfully validating its shape, does NOT constitute approval to apply anything. `root` below is a placeholder (`<TARGET_ROOT>`); until it is replaced with the actual target directory's absolute path, `validate-plan.mjs` returns FAIL on this file — that is intentional, not a defect. Applying any of the changes below to a real repository requires that repository's owner to explicitly approve this exact plan content, re-checked against the current state of the target files, in a separate `apply` step. `checks[].approved` is `false` in this sample for the same reason: the sample's existence is not approval.

target.description: Single Rust library crate (not a workspace). No existing Makefile. Developers and CI currently invoke `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, and `cargo doc` directly and separately; there is no single command that runs all of them, and CI and the pre-commit hook have drifted (CI runs `--all-features`, the hook does not).

adoptedEntryPoint.role: thin entry point only — Make does not become the dependency-graph source of truth for compilation
adoptedEntryPoint.rationale: The crate's real incremental build graph (source files, Cargo.lock, feature flags) is already owned by Cargo and re-implementing it in Make would duplicate that graph and risk drifting from it. Make is adopted only to give a single, memorable, OS-portable set of names (`make check`, `make verify`) that both the developer shell, the Git hook, and CI call, instead of three places independently listing the same four cargo invocations.

sourceOfTruth.notes: Unchanged by this plan; Make never touches target/ or Cargo.lock directly.

sourceOfTruth.concern: lint rule set (clippy lints, fmt config)
sourceOfTruth.notes: Unchanged; Make only invokes the existing configuration.

sourceOfTruth.concern: public command names and their scope
sourceOfTruth.notes: The only thing this plan actually centralizes.

commandContract.name: help
commandContract.purpose: List public commands and how to run each one without Make.

commandContract.name: check
commandContract.purpose: Fast local feedback: formatting check + clippy. Does not run tests.
commandContract.sideEffects: none (read-only; writes only to Cargo's own target/ build cache)

commandContract.name: verify
commandContract.purpose: Full required validation: everything in check, plus unit/integration tests and doctests.
commandContract.sideEffects: none to source; writes to target/ build cache

entryPoints.direct: cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-targets && cargo test --doc

commandContract.notes: cargo test --all-targets does not run doctests; both invocations are required, deliberately not deduplicated by dropping one.

commandContract.name: fix
commandContract.purpose: Auto-fix formatting only. Never invoked automatically by verify/check.
commandContract.sideEffects: rewrites source files in place via cargo fmt

commandContract.name: clean
commandContract.purpose: Remove Cargo's target/ build cache only.
commandContract.sideEffects: deletes target/ (regenerable build output only, nothing under src/)

changes.description: New thin Makefile: .PHONY help/check/verify/fix/clean targets, each a one-line delegation to the cargo invocation already listed above. .DEFAULT_GOAL := help (non-destructive default).
Replace the existing 4 separate `cargo ...` steps with a single `run: make verify` step, so CI and the hook stop drifting. Trigger/job matrix untouched.

Point the existing pre-commit command at `make check` instead of its current inline `cargo fmt --check` one-liner (clippy was previously missing from the hook; this closes that gap intentionally, called out under risks below).

Replace the four separately-documented cargo commands with a pointer to `make help`, keeping the direct cargo commands as the documented non-Make fallback (per this Skill's requirement that Make never becomes a hard dependency for using the crate).

keepExisting: Cargo.lock is committed and remains the lockfile of record; this plan does not change --locked/--offline policy.
CI continues to run on the same trigger events and runner OS; only the step body is consolidated.

addedDependencies.name: GNU Make
addedDependencies.kind: build-time tool, developer machine + CI runner
addedDependencies.reason: Required to use `make <target>`; every target also has a documented direct-cargo fallback so Make is not a hard requirement to build, test, or contribute to the crate.
addedDependencies.alreadyPresent: assumed present on CI's ubuntu-latest image; must be confirmed on each contributor's machine before relying on `make help` in onboarding docs (see verificationPlan.staticOnly below).

risks.description: The pre-commit hook currently only runs `cargo fmt --check`; switching it to `make check` adds clippy to every commit, which is slower and may surface previously-uncaught lint failures on the next commit after this change lands.
risks.mitigation: Call this out explicitly in the PR description introducing the Makefile; do not silently widen hook scope without a heads-up, per this Skill's guidance on hook/CI drift.

risks.description: A contributor's local `make` may be a different implementation/version (e.g. an old GNU Make, or none at all) than assumed.
risks.mitigation: README fallback commands remain the source of truth for what each target actually runs; `make` is convenience, not a gate contributors are blocked by.

alternatives.name: cargo-only, no Makefile
alternatives.description: Keep documenting the four commands in README only, with no single aggregate command.
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Does not solve the observed CI/hook drift (the two already disagree today); a named contract with one definition removes the drift's root cause.

alternatives.name: cargo xtask
alternatives.description: Add a `cargo xtask verify` binary instead of a Makefile.
alternatives.whyNotChosen: For a single, simple library crate with no cross-platform packaging or multi-step orchestration need, an xtask binary is more machinery (its own crate, its own compile step) than the four-command aggregation actually requires; reconsider if the crate later needs conditional/native-Windows-specific steps beyond what a one-line Makefile recipe expresses.

migrationSteps.action: Add Makefile with help/check/verify/fix/clean, each delegating to the existing cargo invocations verbatim (no behavior change yet).
Run `make verify` locally and confirm its output matches running the four cargo commands separately (same pass/fail, same warnings).
Update README to document `make help` alongside the existing direct cargo commands (fallback retained, not removed).
Update .github/workflows/ci.yml to call `make verify` in place of the four separate steps; keep the rest of the job unchanged.
Update .lefthook.yml to call `make check`; note the widened hook scope (clippy added) in the same PR description.

staticOnly: Confirm the target's GNU Make version and platform before assuming .PHONY/tab-recipe syntax used in the drafted Makefile is supported (per this Skill's execution/gnu-posix-bsd-compatibility.md).
Confirm no existing Makefile already exists at the target root (this plan assumes creation, not replacement).
verificationPlan.note: The executable verification commands themselves are the machine-readable `checks` array at the top level of this plan (not duplicated here); see `checks[].name == "verify"`.

approval.approvalMechanism: Explicit user sign-off on this plan's filesToChange list, given after re-reading the target files' current state at apply time.
